documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 62 y/o man, here to establish. Prior PCP retiring; records requested.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes for a long time, managed on glipizide alone as long as he can remember. Checks sugars a few mornings a week, mostly 130s-160s fasting. No lows he can recall. Told several years ago his kidneys were 'stage 3' and that the blood pressure pills protect them. BP pills are metoprolol and lisinopril; takes them reliably. No chest pain on exertion, no dyspnea, no edema. No foot sores. Eyes: had a cataract out earlier this year, vision good since.

PMH: T2DM; CKD 3b; HTN.
PSH: appendectomy at 12; cataract surgery 2022.
Meds (bottles reviewed): glipizide 5 daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 BID, lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: PENICILLIN - anaphylaxis (remote; he was told never to take it again).
FH: father T2DM and a stroke; mother HTN and kidney disease; brother has coronary disease.
SH: retired from the postal service after a long career carrying mail. Married, lives with his wife in South Hadley. Smoked about a pack a day for 30 years, stopped around 2017. A drink once or twice a month. Walks the neighborhood most days.

Exam: BP and vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, well-healed RLQ scar. Feet: skin intact, no calluses or wounds, DP and PT pulses 2+ both feet. No edema.

A/P
1. Type 2 diabetes - on sulfonylurea only. A1c, CMP, urine albumin/Cr today. Continue glipizide 5.
2. CKD 3b - CMP today; prior records will show trend. Continue ACE inhibitor.
3. HTN - near goal today. Continue metoprolol and lisinopril.
4. Statin/aspirin - continue.
5. Former heavy smoker - eligible for annual lung cancer screening CT; discussed what it involves and the chance of a false positive; he wants it. Ordered.
6. Health maintenance - PCV20 given today. Hep C and HIV once. Colonoscopy and tetanus per old records. Flu and COVID in October.

RTC 3 months, sooner as needed. He has the practice number for calls or texts.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Frederick, your labs from Tuesday are back. Your A1c is a bit above where I'd like it but in the range we'd expect on your current medicine. Kidney function is in the stage 3b range, which fits with what you were told before; once your old records arrive I can see whether it has been steady. Potassium is fine. Cholesterol numbers look good on the atorvastatin. Urine protein check was normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. We'll recheck the sugar and kidney numbers at your December visit.

Re: Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959

Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis).
Meds: glipizide, metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - Internal Medicine
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - INTERNAL MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959
Admitted 3/18/2025 via ED. Discharged 3/24/2025 to home.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (anaphylaxis); CEFAZOLIN (rash, pruritus - added this admission).

Reason for admission: chronic right plantar diabetic foot ulcer with new surrounding soft-tissue infection - erythema and warmth around the wound - requiring IV antibiotics and inpatient glucose management.

Hospital course:
1. Right plantar foot ulcer with soft-tissue infection. Foot films without osteomyelitis. Treated with IV vancomycin, levels followed with his kidney function. Erythema receded steadily. Changed to oral doxycycline for discharge.
2. Type 2 diabetes. Glipizide held; basal-bolus insulin with frequent fingersticks. A1c 8.2%. Fasting glucose 156, post-meal 198 on 3/20. After nocturnal low readings the insulin doses were reduced on 3/20.
3. Fever and drug reaction. Shortly after midnight on hospital day 3 (night of 3/20-3/21) he spiked to 38.4 C. The covering physician ordered a dose of IV cefazolin; within the hour he developed an itchy rash. Cefazolin was stopped; the rash and itching resolved over the following day without airway symptoms. Recorded as allergic reaction to cefazolin with penicillin cross-sensitivity. Fever did not recur.
4. Hypoglycemia. Morning fingerstick 48 mg/dL on 3/21, treated with oral glucose with prompt recovery; insulin reduced further. No further lows.
5. Hypertension. Metoprolol continued; BP 132/86 on arrival and controlled throughout. Lisinopril continued.
6. CKD 3b. Creatinine at his usual baseline during the stay.

Discharge medications: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 10 days (new); resume glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily. Insulin stopped at discharge.
Follow-up: PCP within one week; podiatry within 2-4 weeks. Continue offloading boot and daily dressings.

conditions.label: Allergic reaction to cefazolin due to penicillin cross-sensitivity

documents.title: Discharge summary review
documents.author: PCP

2. Cefazolin reaction - resolved. Allergy list now reads penicillin (anaphylaxis) and cefazolin (rash, itching). Told him to mention both at every pharmacy and any hospital.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN RECORD
Patient: Frederick Esposito, 65M  DOB 11/15/1959
Arrival 7/12/2025 07:45, sent in by his primary care physician.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), cefazolin (rash).
Home meds: glipizide 5 daily, metoprolol 50 BID, lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, ASA 81.
PMH: T2DM, CKD 3b, HTN, chronic R plantar diabetic ulcer (infected ulcer admission March).

HPI: 3 days of fever with rigors, right flank pain, dysuria and urinary frequency.

Triage: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 150/90, HR 98, RR 20.
Exam: uncomfortable, nontoxic. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. Lungs clear. Right foot dressing clean, ulcer without surrounding erythema.

Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 13.2. BUN 40, creatinine 2.2 (baseline 1.6). UA: pyuria, leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite positive.

ED course: urine culture sent before antibiotics. IV fluid bolus, then maintenance. Empiric IV aztreonam, selected because of his penicillin anaphylaxis and cefazolin reaction.

Impression: acute pyelonephritis; acute kidney injury on CKD 3b.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - pyelonephritis
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Frederick Esposito  DOB 11/15/1959. Admitted 7/12/2025 from the ED; discharged 7/20/2025 home.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis; cefazolin - rash.

Diagnoses: acute pyelonephritis, E. coli, multidrug resistant; acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3b.

Course: Started on IV fluids and empiric aztreonam in the ED. Renal ultrasound 7/13 showed no hydronephrosis. On 7/14 the urine culture grew E. coli resistant to several classes but sensitive to aminoglycosides. In light of his renal function and the susceptibility pattern, therapy changed to IV gentamicin with once-daily dosing adjusted for kidney function and trough levels monitored. Afebrile from 7/14; flank pain resolved. Seven days of active therapy completed in hospital - no oral antibiotic at discharge.
Creatinine 2.2 on arrival, 2.0 on 7/16, 1.9 on 7/20 (baseline 1.6). Lisinopril held during the admission, resumed at discharge.

Discharge medications: unchanged home list - glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with repeat BMP.

documents.title: ICU and hospital discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL - PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE / MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Frederick Esposito, 66M, DOB 11/15/1959
Admitted 1/17/2026 via the ED to the medical ICU; ward from 1/20; discharged home 1/27/2026.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (anaphylaxis); CEFAZOLIN (rash, itching).
Home medications on admission: glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Relevant history: type 2 diabetes; CKD stage 3b (baseline creatinine 1.6); hypertension; chronic right plantar diabetic ulcer under podiatry care; cefazolin reaction March 2025; multidrug-resistant E. coli pyelonephritis July 2025.

Presentation: per his wife, two days of fever, chills and confusion, progressively less responsive, little oral intake. On arrival T 39.2 C, BP 85/50, HR 120, RR 22. Dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor; lethargic but arousable. WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.0, platelets 150; creatinine 2.5, BUN 50; lactate 5.0. Urinalysis cloudy, leukocyte esterase positive, >50 WBC/hpf. Blood cultures drawn.

Diagnoses: septic shock, urinary source; acute kidney injury on CKD 3b.

Course:
- Shock: supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula, crystalloid boluses, then norepinephrine for persistent hypotension; weaned off 1/19. Lactate 1.6 on 1/18.
- Infection: empiric IV aztreonam and gentamicin, chosen around his beta-lactam allergies and his prior isolate. Urine culture grew E. coli with the same resistance pattern as July; blood cultures no growth. Narrowed to gentamicin, dosed by levels for his kidney function; 10 days completed in hospital. Renal ultrasound without hydronephrosis.
- Kidney: creatinine peaked at admission and was 2.0 at discharge. Lisinopril HELD.
- Mental status back to his baseline before discharge. Metoprolol held during shock, resumed at home dose on the ward. Glipizide held while he was not eating, resumed before discharge.

Discharge medications: glipizide 5 mg daily, metoprolol tartrate 50 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily. HOLD lisinopril until kidney function is rechecked by his PCP.
Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks with BMP. Podiatry as scheduled.

documents.title: Call from patient's wife
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: His wife called the practice line. Frederick has been feverish with chills for two days, increasingly confused and not eating; this morning she could barely get him to answer her, so she called 911. He is in the ICU at the area hospital with an infection - she was told it is from his urine and that his blood pressure is very low. Spoke with the ICU team by phone and gave them his allergy history (penicillin anaphylaxis, cefazolin rash) and the July culture result. Asked his wife to keep us posted; we'll get the records.

documents.body: This is his wife writing on his account. Fred has been home a week. He's weak and sleeping a lot but eating better and he knows what day it is again. The hospital said to see you and get blood work. He's taking everything except the lisinopril like they said. What should we do?

documents.title: RE: Fred is home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for the update - I'm glad he's home. I read the hospital summary. I'd like to see him in the next week or two and repeat his kidney labs then; we'll decide about the lisinopril at that visit. Our front desk will call to set it up. If he has fever, confusion, lightheadedness or isn't drinking, call or text right away.
